case_analysis.apparent_benchmark_claim: The visible case materials appear to ask the agent to read the trip-expense notes in Simple Note and record those expenses in the already-created matching Splitwise groups. The visible note/group inventory includes seven expense trips: Bali, Paris, Honolulu, Budapest, Zurich, London, and Moscow.
case_analysis.actual_checked_outcome: The released evaluator checked a narrower hidden target: all added Splitwise expenses and expense shares had to match private-data maps keyed only by groups 274-278. Adding the visible London and Moscow trip expenses in groups 279 and 280 made tests 003-007 fail.
case_analysis.target_construction_review: `official/ground_truth/private_data.json` encodes only five groups even though the visible initial state includes seven trip-expense notes and seven matching Splitwise groups. That hidden subset construction is what creates the outcome difference.
case_analysis.evaluator_oracle_review: `official/ground_truth/evaluation.py::evaluate` registers ten tests. Tests 003-007 compare all added expenses and expense shares against the hidden private-data maps; because those maps omit groups 279 and 280, the evaluator treats London/Moscow additions as failures. The non-test `test.task_completed` assignment does not alter scoring.
case_analysis.reward_wiring_aggregation_review: No separate reward predicate changed the per-record outcome. `TestTracker.success` is `pass_count == num_tests`, `run_official_job` serializes that tracker, `run_slot` carries the worker summary, and the post-score join reads `native_evaluator_output.json::tracker.success` directly.

official_benchmark_assessment.description: The hidden official target omits the visible London and Moscow trip note/group pairs, so the released evaluator checks only five trips even though the benchmark appears to ask for all visible trip-expense notes to be recorded.

checklist_and_case_packet_assessment.description: The native checklist preserves the official ten registered tests, but the frozen case packet and stronger checklist define 'applicable trip notes' using only `official/dbs/simple_note.jsonl::L1-L10`, excluding the visible London and Moscow notes without source support. That narrower subset is not justified by the visible case materials.

records.different_outcome_description: The benchmark appeared to ask Agent A to record all visible trip-expense notes with matching Splitwise groups, including London and Moscow, but the released evaluator instead required all added expenses to match hidden private-data maps for only groups 274-278 and therefore failed the record for adding groups 279 and 280.
records.reason: The retained API log and end-state Splitwise DB show that Agent A recorded the visible London and Moscow expenses in groups 279 and 280. The native evaluator then failed tests 003-007 because its hidden target only covered groups 274-278. That is a checked outcome different from the visible task claim.

The blind native scorer treated raw `expenses_fts` SQL inserts as proof that `changed_model_names()` included an extra scored model, but the pinned helper semantics enumerate registered model classes rather than arbitrary SQL tables. The cited blind evidence does not support its contradiction claim for test 002.

The blind stronger scorer marked both stronger conditions supported even though the same blind evidence shows extra task-created London and Moscow expenses in groups 279 and 280; under the checklist text, those extra created expenses are not all bound to the checklist's own 'applicable source-note' rows.
